correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the Franklin graph and distance-two clique graph independently. The 12-vertex flag complex has exact face vector (12,48,76,45,12,2), with 20 six-vertex nonedge-perfect-matching octahedral induced subcomplexes. Its signed second and third simplicial boundaries have modular ranks 37 and 35; these give only rational bounds. An independent integer construction formed 35 third-boundary columns plus four oriented octahedral cycles, with full 76-row integer matrix Smith diagonal consisting entirely of 39 units, establishing a primitive rank-39 sublattice of C2. All remaining third boundaries lie in the 35-generated image by the inspected exact-expansion proof; the 39-cycle rank upper bound from ∂2 shows full integral ker ∂2, whence H2=Z^4. Orbit enumeration gives automorphism group size48 and support-orbit sizes8 and12; exact integral coordinate Smith profiles are (1,1,1,1) and (1,1,1). Therefore only the eight orbit spans the full homology and the twelve orbit is a saturated rank-three subgroup; every octahedron coordinate is primitive. The general six-vertex lower-bound lemma for nonzero H2 of a flag complex uses vertex links/Mayer–Vietoris and unique octahedral equality case; this justifies minimal supports rather than relying solely on enumeration. No homotopy-type or infinite-family result was inferred.

value.rationale: The Franklin graph is a canonical symmetric graph; its scale-two Rips/independence complex is a natural finite object whose geometric minimal H2-support cycles have clear combinatorial meaning. Two large automorphism orbits of equally primitive six-vertex spheres have radically different integral spanning power, a nontrivial lattice refinement invisible to the Betti number or symmetry orbit sizes alone. The exhaustive 924-subset classification plus exact Smith lattices is self-contained and useful for integral geometric generators and equivariant Rips calculations despite no general family theorem.

final_claim: For the graph-metric scale-two flag Rips complex of the Franklin graph, H2(K;Z)=Z^4. Exactly 20 induced six-vertex octahedral spheres are minimal nonzero H2 supports; all are primitive. The 48-element automorphism group splits them into size-eight and size-twelve orbits; the eight orbit spans all Z^4, while the twelve orbit spans a primitive rank-three sublattice with quotient Z.
